text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz sent back to Parliament an amendment to the Privatisation Act.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn, in a lengthy interview with the German weekly Der Spiegel, said only NATO can safeguard the security of Europe.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs is scheduled to meet Palestinian Yasser Arafat in Betlehem today. Further Israeli investment and establishment of joint ventures were at the centre of discussions with Israeli businessmen yesterday.
- The Capital's Metropolitan Court will try the series of charges and counter-charges among various Christian Democrat factions this Tuesday.

- A delegation of the Holy See expressed its disagreement Friday with a provision of the income tax law allowing taxpayers to allocate 1 percent of their taxes to a church or charity of their choice. (Sat.)
- The Defence Ministry announced Friday that six countries will stage a joint international military cooperation exercise in Hungary June 17-20. (Sat.)

- A total of 20,000 employees are expected to be fired in the first half of 1997, the number of those leaving the job on their own initiative or by mutual agreement may exceed 40,000. It is estimated that more than 84,000 people will find work.
- Janos Balogh, acting head of the Budapest Police, ordered disciplinary proceedings Friday after nine automatic pistols were found stolen from the 2nd District police station.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The relevant chapter for this year's budget has increased the sum of subsidy granted to political parties by more than 20 percent. (Sat.)

- The major Hungarian companies expected to be privatised include the national oil and gas company MOL, the electricity works MVM and power plant companies Bakonyi Eromu, Vertes Eromu and Pecsi Eromu.
- The Budapest Stock Exchange ranked third in the world in terms of value increase in 1996, Morgan Stanley Capital International reports.
- Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky Friday outlined plans for the capital's development projects, noting that 25 billion forints of the 160 billion forint budget would be spent on development.
- Hungarian environmentalist Gyorgy Biro has been elected one of ten outstanding young people of the world at an annual conference of the Junior Chamber International in Seoul.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The successor organisations of the Arrow Cross, the Hungarian nazi party which ruled the country in 1944, plan a festive commemoration early this week to mark the centenary of the birth of party leader Ferenc Szalasi, who was executed in 1946. Authorities said there is no legal ground for banning such a commemoration.
- The Ministry of Agriculture finalised the agricultural subsidy regime for 1997 yesterday. (Sat.)
NAPI GAZDASAG
- EBRD set up an ECU 30 million fund for the reconstruction of medium-sized, viable but under-funded Hungarian companies.
- Mlada Fronta newspaper of Prague said in its weekend edition that Hungary is the only East European reformist country in which living standards dropped last year.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The insurance company AB-Aegon has won the open tender for an insurance package for the national prison authority. Providencia has won the tender to provide life and accident insurance for police, customs and firefighting personnel.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
